## claude.ai hal2-mcp-hemma
This MCP server controls devices at location: Hemma. Always call the appropriate tool to fetch live data — never rely on previously seen results. Device states, presence, sensor values and scene status can change at any time. When in doubt, call get_all_states or the relevant tool again before answering. Available tools: get_all_states, get_state, get_history, control_device, control_fan, get_scenes, activate_scene, control_cover, control_spa, control_climate, get_presence, get_alerts, set_light, analyze_patterns, get_flow, deploy_flow.

## claude.ai hal2-mcp-landet
This MCP server controls devices at location: Landet. Always call the appropriate tool to fetch live data — never rely on previously seen results. Device states, presence, sensor values and scene status can change at any time. When in doubt, call get_all_states or the relevant tool again before answering. Available tools: get_all_states, get_state, get_history, control_device, get_scenes, activate_scene, control_cover, control_climate, get_presence, get_alerts, set_light, analyze_patterns, get_flow, deploy_flow.

## claude.ai integrations-hemma
This server provides real-time contextual information about the user's environment, location, schedule and iRobot Roomba integration.

Always fetch fresh data — never rely on previously seen results. Weather, pollen and calendar data can change frequently.

Tool guidance:
- get_time: use whenever current time or date is needed, even if it seems implicit.
- get_place: detailed information about the MCP server location.
- get_weather: use for questions about temperature, rain, wind, forecast or outdoor conditions at the MCP server's location. Pair with get_place if location is ambiguous.
- get_pollen: use for pollen levels at the MCP server location, allergy risk, or "is it a good day to be outside" questions.
- get_maja_schedule: use for questions about Maja's activities, school hours, or when she is available. Treat schedule data as potentially sensitive.
- get_calendar_events: use for the family's appointments, meetings, and events. When the user asks "what's happening today/this week", call this.
- get_url: use when the user explicitly provides a URL, or when other tools refer to a URL for additional detail. Can only handle GET. Do not construct or guess URLs.
- irobot_status — Gets current status: cycle, phase, battery%, cleaning time, m², and pmap_id (map ID required for room cleaning).
- irobot_action — Sends a command: start, stop, pause, dock, resume.
- irobot_clean_room — Cleans specific rooms. Requires pmap_id (from irobot_status) and region_ids (array of room IDs). Optional: ordered (clean in order, default true), user_pmapv_id.

When answering questions that span multiple tools (e.g. "is it a good day to go outside and do I have time?"), call the relevant tools in parallel before answering.

 Available tools: get_url, get_time, get_place, get_pollen, get_weather, get_maja_schedule, get_calendar_events, irobot_status, irobot_action, irobot_clean_room.

## claude.ai integrations-landet
Calibre-Web integration for browsing and managing the ebook library. Use calibre_search to find books by title, author or keyword — it returns book IDs needed by other tools. calibre_stats gives a quick library overview. calibre_get_cover fetches the cover image and displays it inline — call it when showing search results unless explicitly asked not to. calibre_toggle_read marks a book as read or unread; the first call after a restart will trigger a login that takes a moment.

Docker integration for managing containers on the Landet server. docker_list shows running containers (all=true includes stopped). docker_start, docker_stop and docker_restart control containers by name. docker_logs fetches recent output — useful for diagnosing problems. Always confirm with the user before stopping or restarting a container.
 Available tools: calibre_search, calibre_stats, calibre_toggle_read, calibre_get_cover, calibre_recent, docker_list, docker_start, docker_stop, docker_restart, docker_logs.

## claude.ai media-hemma
This server manages music playback and audio announcements in the home. Audio is distributed via Music Assistant (port 8095), which streams over AirPlay 2 to all speakers — both HomePods and Sonos (Sonos appear via the AirPlay provider, exposed as universal_player in API).

Speaker workflow: always call music_set_outputs before starting playback to select which rooms should receive audio. The first speaker in the list becomes the sync leader; the rest are joined as group members. If the user does not specify rooms, ask — do not assume all speakers should be active.

Use music_player (action: status) to check current state before acting. If music is already playing, prefer changing track or adjusting volume over stopping and restarting.

music_play accepts either a Spotify/Apple Music URI or a free-text query — when a query is given, the system prefers library entries, then Spotify, then Apple Music. Local library entries (library://...) are curated by the user and considered authoritative.

music_dstm toggles "Don't Stop The Music" — when enabled, MA auto-extends the queue with similar tracks. music_repeat sets loop modes. music_set_volume controls per-speaker volume; music_player controls group volume.

tts_speak speak text aloud on one or more speakers via Music Assistant. Use device name (e.g. "kök", "kontor"), comma-separated list, or "all". Device names are matched against Music Assistant player display names.

Prefer specific room names matching music_get_outputs.

Available tools: tts_speak, music_get_outputs, music_set_outputs, music_play, music_player, music_set_volume, music_search, music_dstm, music_repeat. Available tools: tts_speak, music_get_outputs, music_set_outputs, music_play, music_player, music_set_volume, music_search, music_dstm, music_repeat, music_favorite.

## claude.ai media-landet
This server manages the media library and request pipeline. Seerr is the entry point for requesting content — it routes TV requests to Sonarr and movie requests to Radarr. Use Sonarr and Radarr to check what is actually downloaded and available.

Checking availability:

Movie: radarr_search → hasFile: true means it is in the library.
TV series overview: seerr_search → status field shows overall availability.
TV per season: seerr_get_tv → seasons[].status.
TV individual episodes: sonarr_get_series to get the Sonarr series ID, then sonarr_get_episodes with season_number → hasFile per episode.
Requesting content:
Use seerr_search to find the title and get its TMDB ID and mediaType, then seerr_request to submit the request. For TV shows, call seerr_get_tv first to identify which seasons are missing before requesting. Check status afterwards with seerr_get_requests.

Posters:
Search results include a poster URL — display it inline when presenting results unless asked not to.

Downloads and upcoming:
sonarr_get_queue shows active TV downloads. sonarr_get_calendar shows upcoming episodes. There is no equivalent queue tool for Radarr.

This server also manages music playback and audio announcements in the home. Audio is distributed via Music Assistant (port 8095), which streams over AirPlay 2 to all speakers — both HomePods and Sonos (Sonos appear via the AirPlay provider, exposed as universal_player in API).

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

content.text:
Bekräftat. Buggen stämmer. Här är vad som händer:

**Live-svaret** för Terrass Väderstation ovan saknar `tags` på thing-nivå, fast enheten har taggar konfigurerade. (Item-nivåns `notes` kommer med, men inga thing-taggar.)

**Rotorsaken** är enkel. I [thing.js:80-83](core/thing.js#L80-L83) läses config in i noden:

```js
this.name = config.name;
this.notes = config.notes;
this.topicPrefix = config.topicPrefix;
this.attributes = config.attributes;
```

`config.tags` läses aldrig in — det finns ingen `this.tags = config.tags`. Editorn sparar taggarna ([thing.html:348](core/thing.html#L348) sparar `node.tags` som array), men runtime-noden plockar aldrig upp dem.

Sedan i [eventhandler.js:575](core/eventhandler.js#L575):

```js
if (Array.isArray(thing.tags) && thing.tags.length) deviceEntry.tags = thing.tags;
```

Eftersom `thing.tags` är `undefined` är `Array.isArray(...)` alltid `false`, så taggarna kommer aldrig med i `deviceEntry`. Det gäller alltså inte bara `get_state` utan `getAllStates()` i sin helhet — så `get_all_states` har samma blinda fläck.

Item-taggarna fungerar för att de läses från thingType-noden (`itm.tags`), inte från thing-noden.

Fixen är en rad i thing.js:

```js
this.notes = config.notes;
this.tags = config.tags || [];   // ny rad
```

Vill du att jag lägger in den? Det är en ren one-liner, men jag deployar inget till Node-RED utan att du säger till.

content.text:
Hmm. Taggarna kcommer fortfarande inte med — svaret ovan saknar `tags` på thing-nivå.

Det säger mig något: ändringen jag gjorde ligger i [thing.js](core/thing.js), som är **runtime-kod för noden**. Node-RED laddar nodmodulerna när processen startar. En vanlig flow-**deploy** kör inte om `require` på modulen — den gamla `thing.js` snurrar fortfarande, och `this.tags` är fortfarande `undefined`.

Med andra ord: en flödesdeploy räcker inte här. Node-RED-processen behöver startas om för att den nya `thing.js` ska läsas in.

Två saker att kolla:

1. **Startade du om hela Node-RED**, eller gjorde du bara en Deploy i editorn? Om bara deploy — starta om runtimen och så testar jag igen.
2. Om du redan startat om och det ändå inte funkar, då är nästa misstänkta att enheten faktiskt inte har taggar sparade i sin config. Då kan jag titta närmare på om `config.tags` verkligen persisteras från [thing.html](core/thing.html).

Vill du starta om runtimen så kör jag verifieringen igen?
Aha, det var ett orelaterat problem med en symlänk som hade försvunnit. Testa igen.

Där har vi det. Längst ner i svaret nu:

```json
"tags": [
  "outdoor"
]
```

Thing-taggarna kommer med i `get_state`. Buggen är borta — `this.tags = config.tags || []` plockas upp och guarden i [eventhandler.js:575](core/eventhandler.js#L575) släpper igenom dem. Samma sak gäller `get_all_states` eftersom de delar `getAllStates()`.

Allt verifierat mot den riktiga enheten. Snyggt jobbat med symlänken — den typen av fel kan lura en rejält.
